title: Escape hatches are reported under one rule id
what: `anvil check` reports @ts-ignore, eslint-disable, # type: ignore, # noqa, #[allow], unsafe, PHP @ and !important as `no-escape-hatches`, not under their per-kind ids such as no-ts-ignore. Tier 0 lines look like `[ERROR] path:l:c [rule]` and Tier 1 lines like `[ERROR] [rule] path:l —`.
why: Benchmark expectations and any tooling that parses check output must use the reported ids and accept both line formats.
learned: The slop benchmark documents the known gaps no-swallowed-errors, no-commented-out-code and TS no-debug-helpers. Close them by adding a rule and moving the case from known-gap to expect.
author: reactive-end
